title: Planning the dusting sequence from high points down
audience: Cleaners who dust offices, shared rooms and reception areas on a scheduled route.
learningOutcomes: Explain why high points are dusted before lower surfaces.
Plan a dusting route that uses each tool once per pass.
Walk a room in one direction so that no surface is dusted twice.

instruction.heading: Why order matters
instruction.body: Dust that falls from a high surface lands on work you have already finished. Working from a room's highest point downward, and from the far side back toward the entry, keeps completed areas clean and stops you from covering the same ground twice. The order is a method, not a preference.

instruction.heading: Sequencing the tools
instruction.body: Begin at the storage room with protective equipment on. Take the extension duster first for the high work, then return to collect the cloths, the brush and the polish for desk-level work. Going back and forth costs time, so plan the sequence to use each tool once per pass.

instruction.heading: Moving through the space
instruction.body: Walk the room in one direction, moving between rows and cubicles in short passes. Watch ceiling corners, light fittings, ledges and sills as you go. Finish with the lower surfaces and the floor-level furniture, then return the tools to storage.

procedure: Put on protective equipment at the storage room.
Take the extension duster and dust the high points as you walk the route.
Return to storage, and set up cloths, brush, polish and apron for the desk-level work.
Dust desks, shelves and furniture from the top surfaces downward.
Return the tools and set the cloths aside for cleaning.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner dusts a desk first, then notices cobwebs in the ceiling corner above it.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What order should have been followed?
workedExamples.reasoning: High points come first. The corner dust would have dropped onto the desk and forced a second pass. The high-first order puts falling dust onto surfaces that are dusted later, so it is removed in one go.

commonErrors.error: Dusting desks before ceilings and corners.
commonErrors.prevention: Dust the high points first on every route.

commonErrors.error: Walking the same area twice because the tools were carried in the wrong order.
commonErrors.prevention: Plan the route as one loop and take each tool once per pass.
Return each item to its place as soon as its surface is done.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Never climb onto furniture to reach a high point. Use an extension tool from a steady position on the floor.
Wear eye protection while dusting overhead, because dust and debris fall downward.

qualityStandard: High points are dusted before desk-level work.
No surface is dusted twice on one route.
Items are returned to their original positions.
documentationEvidence: Dusting route completion noted on the job sheet.
summary: Dust high points first so falling dust is removed when the lower work is done.
Plan the route as one loop, using each tool once per pass.
Put items back where they were, and never climb onto furniture to reach high areas.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why are high areas dusted before lower areas?
options: So falling dust is removed when the lower surfaces are done
Because high dusting is charged at a higher hourly rate
Because ceilings need cloths and desks do not

knowledgeChecks.question: A route passes the same desks twice because the tools were carried in the wrong order. What is the fix?
options: Skip the desks on the second pass to save time
Plan the route so each tool is used once per pass
Dust faster on the opening pass and move on quickly
